claim: Hwangbo et al. 2019 train ANYmal command-conditioned locomotion using TRPO on a single desktop PC (1 CPU + 1 GPU) with the policy converging in approximately 4 hours wall clock.
stance_target: pre-GPU-parallelism era locomotion RL required hours on modest single-machine hardware
scope_conditions: ANYmal quadruped, RaiSim-family simulator with actuator nets, TRPO algorithm, circa 2019
quoted_support: For training command-conditioned and high-speed locomotion, TRPO finished training in nine days of simulated time, which corresponds to four hours of computation in real time.

claim: The Hwangbo 2019 simulator with actuator nets runs at ~500K simulation time steps per second on a single desktop, enabling approximately 250M sample generation in 4 hours.
stance_target: simulation speed is the primary bottleneck; faster simulation directly multiplies sample budget in fixed wall-clock time
scope_conditions: Custom RaiSim-based simulator with 12-joint actuator networks; single CPU desktop; not GPU-parallelized
quoted_support: the full hybrid simulator, including a rigid-body simulation and the actuator nets, runs at nearly 500K time steps per second, which allows the simulation to run roughly a thousand times faster than real time.

claim: Hwangbo 2019 uses 30 parallel ANYmal instances with randomized inertial properties for domain randomization — orders of magnitude fewer parallel instances than the later Isaac Gym era (4096).
stance_target: pre-GPU parallelism era used very few parallel instances vs. current practice
quoted_support: we robustify the policy by training with 30 different ANYmal models with stochastically sampled inertial properties.

claim: Hwangbo 2019 requires 'hundreds of millions of samples' to train a complicated legged policy, making fast simulation (not GPU parallelism) the key enabler.
stance_target: legged locomotion RL requires very large sample counts even with simple CPU-based training
quoted_support: Because we need hundreds of millions of samples to train a complicated policy, this solver was key to our work.

claim: Hwangbo 2019 trains with a two-stage pipeline: (1) actuator network pretrain via self-supervised learning (<4 min data collection from 12 physical actuators), then (2) RL policy training (4-11 hours).
stance_target: staged training pipelines (pretrain then RL) are established practice for legged locomotion
scope_conditions: Requires physical robot for actuator net data; ANYmal; 2019
quoted_support: Data collection took less than 4 min since the data can be collected in parallel from the 12 identical actuators on ANYmal. Data was collected at 400 Hz, therefore the resulting dataset contains more than a million samples.
